turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What should I ask when I go to see a flat?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask what's included in the rent, how much bills usually are, and how long the lease is. Also ask why the last tenant left.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Anything I should check myself?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Run the taps and the shower to test the water pressure, look for damp or mould in corners, and check your phone signal in each room.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Phone signal, I never would have thought of that.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's easy to miss. Same with noise, try to visit in the evening if you can.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And if I like it, should I / just say yes on the spot?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: In a busy market you might have to move fast. Have your documents ready so you can apply the same day.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I pack plates so they don't break?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Wrap each one in paper and stand them on their edge in the box, like records. They're much stronger that way than stacked flat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: On their edge? Really?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Really. Put some crumpled paper at the bottom of the box too, and fill any gaps so nothing moves.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about glasses? We have / a lot of wine glasses.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Stuff a bit of paper inside each glass, then wrap the outside. Liquor stores often give away boxes with dividers, which are perfect.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh nice, I'll ask at the shop down the road.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good idea. And mark those boxes fragile on every side, not just the top.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My kids are really upset about moving to a new town.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's understandable, it's a big change. How old are they?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Six and eleven.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Letting them have some say helps a lot. The younger one could choose a paint colour for their room, the older one could help plan the layout.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My eleven year old is mostly sad about / leaving her best friend.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's the hardest part. Plan a visit or a sleepover in the first couple of months, so she knows the friendship doesn't have to end.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's a good idea. They could video call too.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. And finding a club in the new town quickly will help her meet people her age.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Who do I need to tell when I move?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Your bank, your employer, your doctor and dentist, and any utility companies. Don't forget the council and your insurance.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's a lot. Is there a way to do it all at once?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not really, but setting up mail forwarding for a few months catches anything you forget.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good. Oh, and the internet. Should I / set that up before I move in?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, as early as possible. Installation can take a couple of weeks, so book it as soon as you have the address.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll do that today then.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Great. Make a quick checklist too, so you can tick things off as you go.

option_sets.lead_in: We're moving next month and I'm stuck on how to actually do the move.
options: The first option is hiring a full service moving company that packs everything, but it's expensive.
Then there's renting a big truck and getting friends to help in exchange for pizza.
Option three is one of those portable storage containers they drop off and pick up later.
And the last one is hiring movers just for the heavy furniture and packing the rest ourselves.
moshi_comment: Hiring movers just for the heavy stuff is often the sweet spot, you save money and your back. The full service company is worth it if you're short on time. The truck with friends is cheapest, but it depends on how reliable your friends are.
How far are you moving, and do you have a gap between leaving and moving in? If there's a gap, the storage container solves two problems at once. Otherwise I'd go with movers for the heavy furniture.

option_sets.lead_in: I've seen a few apartments and I need to choose one before Friday.
options: One is a bright two bedroom near the train station, but the rent is at the top of my budget.
Another is a cheaper place in a quiet neighborhood, but it's a forty minute bus ride to work.
Or there's a small studio right downtown with a gym in the building and no parking.
moshi_comment: The two bedroom near the station gives you space and an easy commute, if you can handle the rent. The cheaper place saves money but that long bus ride adds up every day. The studio is great for city life if you don't own a car.
Do you work from home at all? If you do, the extra bedroom near the station is really valuable. If not, the studio downtown could be fun and simple.
